Prof. Lenthe is a very organized person, and this organization greatly contributes to the success of the course. Before exams and quizzes, he clearly explains what to expect, which makes studying much easier and more comfortable.
However, he is very strict about his rules such as being late to class—once the door is closed, no one is allowed to enter.

Professor Victor always teaches discussion-based classes. He truly requires active participation, but this participation becomes truly enjoyable, especially if the texts he provides interest you. He also tries to incorporate interactive group work (such as acting out a scene from Shakespeare) which makes the class more enjoyable and engaging. He explains what he expects from assignments beforehand. However, if you don't find this sufficient, it's difficult to communicate with him and get more information. He assumes that what he has written is adequate and prefers not to provide further details. Still, as a student who never used the close reading method in my 111 class, I think learning it and using it in my assignments has been really beneficial for me. His grading isn't overly strict, but I don't think every point deduction is entirely understandable. He certainly doesn't grade based on who the student is, but he fails to adequately explain why he deducts points in some cases. He's also quite strict about the class start time. I don't mind this for regular classes, but I can't understand why he doesn't allow lateness, even for quizzes. According to him, late arrivals disturb students and affect their performance, so he doesn't allow it. However, he also influences performance by giving really really frequent warnings and reminders during the exam. I don't understand the logic behind this. There's a "no technology policy," which I didn't mind because it's a feature I'm used to from almost every course, but it might be difficult for those who follow the lessons on tablets.

Dr. Lenthe is a competent professor, he puts in time and effort, thus, understandably, expects a decent amount of engagement and responsibility from his students.
